purpose: The Notes screen is a dated notebook where the analyst jots quick timestamped notes against a day. The default day is Today, and past or future days can be picked for backfilling. As you type, each note is auto-tagged to projects and BAU routines using case-insensitive substring and alias matching, and each tag chip links to that project or routine. A right rail explains that notes from the last 5 business days go to Remi (the Tell Remi AI update) as background. It also offers one CTA ('Turn this day into an update') that opens the Tell Remi check-in drawer prefilled with the day's notes, a per-day 'Mentioned on this day' tally, and a Mon–Fri 'This week' bar chart. Notes never change the plan directly.
layout:
MOUNT CONTEXT: Rendered by the Remi.dc.html shell inside <main> (to the right of an 88px nav rail, below a 72px header) as <section data-screen-label="Notes" style="position:absolute; inset:0; overflow:hidden">. The <dc-import name="Notes"> is itself position:absolute; inset:0. Available area at the 1920×1080 frame: 1832×1008px. At 2560×1440: 2472×1368px. The shell renders the app at a fixed logical frame size and scales it with transform:scale to fit the window; with 'Fit window' it uses the real viewport.

ROOT: div, height:100%; display:grid; grid-template-columns:300px minmax(0,1fr) 340px; min-height:0. Three columns: LEFT RAIL 300px fixed, CENTER fluid, RIGHT RAIL 340px fixed. The center is 1192px wide at 1920 and 1832px at 2560, but its content is capped at max-width 820px and centred, so the extra width at 2560 becomes side whitespace. Only the rails and the column scroll areas change with frame size.

LEFT RAIL ('Notebook'): min-height:0; display:flex; flex-direction:column; border-right:1px solid var(--hairline).
 - Header block: padding:32px 28px 14px 36px.
   • Kicker 'Notebook': font-size 11px, weight 600, letter-spacing 0.08em, uppercase, color var(--ink-muted).
   • totalLine (e.g. '6 notes across 3 days'): 13px, var(--ink-muted), margin-top 6px.
 - Scroll list: flex:1; min-height:0; overflow-y:auto; overflow-x:hidden; padding:0 16px 24px 20px.
   • Week header (only on the first/latest day of each Mon-based week): padding:18px 16px 6px; font-family var(--font-numeric) (JetBrains Mono); 10px; color var(--ink-faint). Text is 'This week' or 'Week of 28 Sep'.
   • Day row <button>: width 100%; display grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0,1fr) auto; column-gap 10px; align-items baseline; padding 11px 16px 12px; margin-bottom 2px; border 0; border-radius var(--radius-m)=6px; background = selected ? var(--paper-raised) : transparent; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px (selected ? var(--hairline) : transparent); text-align left; cursor pointer; transition: background var(--dur-fast)=140ms var(--ease-out). Hover: background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--ink) 3.5%, transparent) (applied as an !important class, so on hover it overrides even the selected paper-raised background).
       – Col 1: label span, 14px, font-weight 600 if selected else 500, color var(--ink) if the day has notes or is selected, else var(--ink-muted). Text is 'Today · Mon 5 Oct' for today, otherwise 'Fri 2 Oct'.
       – Col 2: count span, JetBrains Mono 11px, var(--ink-muted), showing the note count or '' when 0.
       – Row 2 (grid-column 1 / -1): preview span, margin-top 4px, font var(--font-display) (Libre Caslon Text) 13px, line-height 1.4, single line (white-space nowrap, overflow hidden, text-overflow ellipsis). Color var(--ink-muted) with normal style when the day has notes; var(--ink-faint) italic when empty.

CENTER COLUMN: min-height:0; overflow-y:auto (the whole page scrolls). Inner page div: max-width 820px; box-sizing border-box; padding 36px 56px 80px; margin 0 auto (text measure = 708px). Opacity and transform are driven by the day-switch animation.
 - Header row: display flex; align-items center; gap 12px; min-height 24px.
   • Kicker (e.g. 'Today', 'Last business day', '3 business days ago', holiday name, or 'Weekend'): 11px/600, letter-spacing 0.08em, uppercase, var(--ink-muted).
   • When the selected day is not today, a back button: display flex; align-items center; gap 4px; height 24px; padding 0 9px 0 5px; border 1px solid var(--hairline); radius var(--radius-s)=3px; background var(--paper-raised); font-size 12px; cursor pointer. Content is a Material Symbols Outlined 'chevron_left' icon (15px) followed by 'Today'.
 - H1 title (e.g. 'Monday 5 October'): margin 12px 0 0; font var(--font-display); weight 400; 48px; line-height 1.1; letter-spacing -0.015em.
 - Sub line (e.g. 'BD3 · 3 notes · Returns · BAU, Returns pipeline, ManCo automation'): 14px, var(--ink-muted), margin-top 12px.
 - COMPOSER row: margin-top 32px; display grid; grid-template-columns 64px minmax(0,1fr); column-gap 8px; align-items start; padding 14px 0 16px; border-top 1px solid var(--ink) (a strong dark rule); border-bottom 1px solid var(--hairline).
   • Col 1: time, JetBrains Mono 12px, var(--ink-faint), padding-top 6px. Shows the live HH:MM when on today, '—:—' otherwise.
   • Col 2: textarea with rows=1; display block; width 100%; box-sizing border-box; min-height 34px; resize none; overflow hidden; field-sizing content (auto-grows); border 0; outline 0; background transparent; padding 3px 0; font var(--font-display) 20px; line-height 1.5; color var(--ink). The placeholder colour comes from a global rule: color-mix(in oklch, var(--ink-faint) 70%, var(--paper)); opacity 1.
   • Below the textarea: a flex row; align-items center; gap 10px; margin-top 6px; min-height 22px (reserved height, so no layout shift). It holds the live draft tag chips (non-interactive spans), a flex:1 spacer, and the hint 'Enter to jot · Shift+Enter for a new line' (12px, var(--ink-faint), opacity 1 only when the trimmed draft is non-empty, otherwise 0).
 - ENTRY rows, newest first. Each row: display grid; grid-template-columns 64px minmax(0,1fr); column-gap 8px; align-items start; padding 14px 0 12px; border-bottom 1px solid var(--hairline); background transparent, or color-mix(in oklch, var(--pc-accent) 7%, transparent) while the note is 'fresh'.
   • Col 1: time 'HH:MM', JetBrains Mono 12px, var(--ink-muted), padding-top 5px.
   • Col 2 (min-width 0): an inline-editable textarea with rows=1; display block; width calc(100% + 12px); margin 0 -6px; padding 2px 6px (a 6px hover/focus pad that keeps the text aligned); box-sizing border-box; resize none; overflow hidden; field-sizing content; border 0; outline 0; background transparent; border-radius 3px; font var(--font-display) 18px; line-height 1.55; var(--ink); transition background 140ms ease-out. Hover: background color-mix(in oklch, var(--ink) 3%, transparent). Focus: background var(--paper-raised) plus box-shadow inset 0 0 0 1px var(--hairline). Both are !important classes, and focus wins over hover.
   • When tags exist, a chip row follows: display flex; flex-wrap wrap; gap 6px; margin-top 6px. Chips are buttons.
 - Empty state (no notes that day): padding 28px 0; var(--font-display) italic 18px; line-height 1.5; var(--ink-muted).

TAG CHIP (identical look in the composer (span) and on entries (button)): display inline-flex; align-items center; gap 6px; height 20px; padding 0 7px; border 0; border-radius 3px; background = tag.soft (var(--pc-accent-soft) or var(--fi-accent-soft), i.e. the accent at 13% mixed into paper); font-size 11px; weight 500; text in the inherited ink colour. A 5×5px circular dot in tag.accent comes first. The entry variant has cursor pointer.

RIGHT RAIL: min-height 0; overflow-y auto; border-left 1px solid var(--hairline); background var(--paper-raised). Inner padding 32px on all sides.
 - Kicker 'Remi reads these' (11px/600/0.08em/uppercase/ink-muted).
 - Paragraph: margin 10px 0 0; 14px; line-height 1.55; var(--ink-muted); text-wrap pretty.
 - CTA button: margin-top 18px; width 100%; height 40px; display flex; centred; gap 8px; border 0; radius 6px; background var(--ink) when the day has notes, else var(--ink-faint); color var(--paper); 14px/600; cursor pointer or default. Content is a Material Symbols 'edit_note' icon (18px) plus the label. There is no hover or active style.
 - remiNote: 12px; var(--ink-muted); margin-top 8px; line-height 1.45.
 - Kicker 'Mentioned on this day', margin-top 34px. List container: margin-top 10px; border-top 1px solid var(--hairline). Rows are buttons: width 100%; display grid; grid-template-columns 10px minmax(0,1fr) auto; column-gap 10px; align-items center; padding 11px 0; border 0; border-bottom 1px solid var(--hairline); background transparent; text-align left; cursor pointer. Each row has a 7×7 dot in the accent, a name (14px/500, ellipsis) and a count ('2 notes', JetBrains Mono 11px, ink-muted). Empty text: 13px; line-height 1.5; ink-muted; padding 10px 0.
 - Kicker 'This week', margin-top 34px. Bar area: display flex; align-items flex-end; gap 6px; height 56px; margin-top 12px. There are 5 buttons (flex 1; height 100%; flex column; justify-content flex-end; gap 6px; transparent; padding 0; cursor pointer; with a title tooltip), each containing a bar span: display block; height = c/maxN×100%; min-height 2px; border-radius 1px; background var(--ink) if selected, var(--ink-faint) if count > 0, var(--hairline) if 0; transition height var(--dur-slow)=440ms var(--spring-soft). Labels row below: display flex; gap 6px; margin-top 6px; each label flex 1, centred, JetBrains Mono 10px, color var(--ink) if selected else var(--ink-muted). Labels read like 'M 5', 'T 6', 'W 7', 'T 8', 'F 9'.

DESIGN TOKENS (from the Remi.dc.html :root):
 - --paper oklch(0.975 0.007 85); --paper-raised oklch(0.99 0.004 85); --ink oklch(0.23 0.012 70); --ink-muted oklch(0.47 0.012 70); --ink-faint oklch(0.58 0.01 75); --hairline oklch(0.9 0.008 80).
 - --pc-accent oklch(0.5 0.1 128); --pc-accent-soft color-mix(in oklch, var(--pc-accent) 13%, var(--paper)); --fi-accent oklch(0.5 0.1 265); --fi-accent-soft likewise.
 - Fonts: --font-ui 'Albert Sans'; --font-display 'Libre Caslon Text', Georgia, serif; --font-numeric 'JetBrains Mono'.
 - --radius-s 3px; --radius-m 6px.
 - --dur-fast 140ms; --dur-base 240ms; --dur-slow 440ms; --ease-out cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1); --spring-soft linear(0, 0.049 5%, 0.156 10%, 0.283 15%, 0.408 20%, 0.522 25%, 0.62 30%, 0.702 35%, 0.769 40%, 0.864 50%, 0.922 60%, 0.956 70%, 0.976 80%, 0.987 90%, 1). Under reduced motion --spring-soft becomes steps(1, jump-start).
 - body font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; buttons, inputs and textareas inherit font and colour.
 - The screenshot is at screenshots/notes.png.

components.name: NotesScreen (root grid)
components.description: A 3-column grid: 300px | minmax(0,1fr) | 340px at full height. It owns all local state, including the selected day, composer draft, in-progress edit drafts, fresh highlight, fade/dir and the clock. It autofocuses the composer 320ms after the app screen switches to 'notes'.

components.name: NotebookHeader
components.description: Kicker 'Notebook' (11px/600/0.08em/uppercase/ink-muted) above totalLine (13px ink-muted, mt 6px), e.g. '6 notes across 3 days'. Padding 32px 28px 14px 36px.

components.name: DayList / WeekHeader / DayRow
components.description: A scrollable list of days in descending order. It covers every business day from TODAY back 27 calendar days, plus any day in that window that has notes (weekends and holidays appear only when they have notes), plus any older day that has notes and falls inside the calendar range. A WeekHeader (mono 10px ink-faint, padding 18px 16px 6px) appears at the first row of each Monday-based week: 'This week' for the current week, otherwise 'Week of {d Mon}'. Each DayRow button shows a label, a count and a one-line display-font preview of the most recently added note. Clicking a row switches day with the fade animation.
states: selected: bg paper-raised, inset 1px hairline ring, label weight 600, ink
has notes: label ink, preview ink-muted normal
empty: label ink-muted, preview ink-faint italic, 'No notes' (or 'Nothing yet today' for today)

components.name: DayPageHeader
components.description: A kicker (relative-day text) with an optional '‹ Today' pill button (24px high, 1px hairline border, 3px radius, paper-raised, 12px text, chevron_left icon at 15px, padding 0 9px 0 5px, gap 4px). Below it an H1 with the long date in 48px Libre Caslon 400, line-height 1.1, tracking -0.015em, margin-top 12px, then a sub line at 14px ink-muted, margin-top 12px: 'BD{n} · {k} note(s)|no notes yet · top-3 mention names'.
states: past BD: 'Last business day' / 'N business days ago'

components.name: Composer
components.description: A 64px time column and a fluid column, with a 1px ink top rule and a 1px hairline bottom rule (padding 14px 0 16px, margin-top 32px). The single-row auto-growing textarea uses Libre Caslon 20px/1.5. Under it sit live tag chips for the draft plus the 'Enter to jot · Shift+Enter for a new line' hint, which fades in (140ms) only when the draft is non-empty. The time shows the live HH:MM (refreshed every 20s) on today and '—:—' on other days. The placeholder is 'Jot something down…' on today and 'Add a note to {Fri 2 Oct}…' on other days. Enter adds the note, Shift+Enter inserts a newline.
states: typing (hint visible, chips appear as aliases match)

components.name: NoteEntry
components.description: A 64px time column plus a column with an inline-editable textarea (Libre Caslon 18px/1.55, a 6px negative-margin pad so the hover/focus background extends beyond the text, 3px radius) and a wrap row of clickable TagChips. Rows show newest first, each with a 1px hairline bottom border and padding 14px 0 12px. A just-added note shows a background of color-mix(in oklch, var(--pc-accent) 7%, transparent) for 1400ms, then fades out over 900ms ease-out. Hovering the row sets the global hover to the first tag's id.

components.name: TagChip
components.description: 20px tall, padding 0 7px, 3px radius, background = tag.soft, 11px/500 text, 6px gap, with a 5px circular accent dot. It is a static span in the composer and a button (cursor pointer, border 0) in entries, where clicking opens the project workspace or the routine. Routine chips are labelled '{short} · BAU' and always use the PC accent.

components.name: EmptyDay
components.description: Italic Libre Caslon 18px/1.5 ink-muted, padding 28px 0. Shown only when the selected day has no notes.

components.name: RemiReadsPanel
components.description: Right rail top section: a kicker, an explanatory paragraph, a full-width 40px CTA with the edit_note icon, and a 12px note that includes the live count of notes from the last 5 business days that Remi will receive.
states: day has notes: ink bg, pointer, label 'Turn this day into an update'
day empty: ink-faint bg, default cursor, label 'Nothing to send yet', click no-op

components.name: MentionsList
components.description: 'Mentioned on this day': one row per distinct tag across the selected day's notes (computed from the saved note text, not unsaved drafts), sorted by note count descending (stable, so ties keep first-seen order: projects before routines within each note, notes in chronological order). Each row has a 7px accent dot, the name (14px/500, ellipsis) and a mono 11px count 'N note(s)'. Rows are separated by hairlines. Clicking opens the target and hovering sets the global hover.
states: empty: 'No projects or routines named yet. Mention one and it is linked here.'

components.name: WeekSpark
components.description: 'This week': 5 vertical bars for Mon–Fri of TODAY's week (plain calendar days, not a business-day check), in a 56px-tall flex row with 6px gaps. Bar height is count/max(3, max count) as a percentage, with a 2px minimum and 1px radius. Labels read '{weekday initial} {date}' in mono 10px. Each bar has a tooltip like 'Mon 5 Oct · 3 notes'. Clicking a bar selects that day, including future days.
states: selected day: bar ink, label ink

dataConsumed: model.notes: Record<isoDate 'YYYY-MM-DD', Array<{ id: string ('n1' | 'n'+Date.now().toString(36)), t: string 'HH:MM' (24h local wall-clock at creation), text: string }>>. Arrays are in insertion order (oldest first). A day key is deleted when its last note is removed.
model.TODAY: number, the integer day number (UTC days since epoch = Math.round(Date.UTC(y,m-1,d)/86400000)), hard-coded to dn('2026-10-05') (Mon 5 Oct 2026, BD3).
model.F formatters: F.iso(n) -> 'YYYY-MM-DD'; F.dn(iso) -> day number; F.s(n) -> 'Mon 5 Oct'; F.l(n) -> 'Monday 5 October'; F.dm(n) -> '5 Oct'; F.wd(n) -> 'Mon'; F.d(n) -> 5 (day of month).

model.CAL: days[n] = { n, iso, w (0=Sun..6=Sat, UTC), m (month 0-11), d, y, bd: boolean business day (Mon–Fri and not in the HOL map), bdm: business-day-of-month index (1-based) or null, hol: holiday name or null }. It covers 2026-08-31..2027-04-30. CAL.bds is a sorted array of business-day numbers. CAL.bdDiff(a,b) = idx[nextBD(b)] - idx[nextBD(a)] (business days from a to b; negative if b is earlier).
HOL (shell): { '2026-12-25': 'Christmas Day', '2026-12-28': 'Boxing Day (substitute)', '2027-01-01': "New Year's Day", '2027-03-26': 'Good Friday', '2027-03-29': 'Easter Monday' }

model.P: derived projects array. Fields used: id, name, short, accent ('var(--pc-accent)' | 'var(--fi-accent)'), soft ('var(--pc-accent-soft)' | 'var(--fi-accent-soft)'). Seed ids: ret 'Returns pipeline automation'/'Returns pipeline'; manco 'ManCo pack automation'/'ManCo automation'; play 'PC handover playbook'/'Handover playbook'; fion 'FI onboarding & data access'/'FI onboarding'; alpha 'Alpha engine v0'/'Alpha engine'.

model.routines: derived routines. Fields used: id, name, short, pid (linked project id). Seeds: r-ret name 'Fund & security-level returns', short 'Returns', pid 'ret'; r-man name 'Managing Committee pack', short 'ManCo pack', pid 'manco'.
model.reduced: boolean, true only when the shell's Motion tweak prop === 'Reduced' (does NOT include the prefers-reduced-motion media query).
model.screen: the current app screen id. Used to detect arrival on 'notes' for autofocus.

Actions: model.addNote(dayIso, text) -> returns the new id; model.updateNote(dayIso, id, text); model.removeNote(dayIso, id); model.openProject(pid); model.openRoutine(rid); model.setHover(id|null); model.openCheckIn(pid|null, prefill {text})

Derived in-file: tagsFor(text) -> Array<{ id, name, accent, soft, open() }>; mentions (aggregated tags with counts); recentN (count of notes over the last 5 business days <= TODAY); total (all notes, all days); dayText (prefill string).
interactions: Arrival: when model.screen changes to 'notes' from any other screen, the composer textarea is focused after setTimeout 320ms (matching the shell's 60ms-delayed 240ms cross-fade).

Click a DayRow in the left list: pick(n). If n is already the current day, nothing happens. Otherwise the page fades out, swaps day at 120ms and fades back in, then the composer is focused 40ms after the swap. Picking TODAY stores sel=null.
Click the '‹ Today' pill (only when not on today): pick(TODAY).
Click a WeekSpark bar: pick(that day). This can select future weekdays of the current week.
Composer typing: a controlled textarea (onChange sets state.draft). Tag chips update live under the input. The hint text fades in when trim(draft) is non-empty.

Composer Enter (without Shift): preventDefault, then addNow(). The draft is trimmed. If empty, nothing happens. Otherwise model.addNote(selectedDayIso, trimmedText) runs, the draft is cleared and fresh=newId is set, then fresh is cleared after 1400ms (resetting any previous timer). The note is stamped with the CURRENT wall-clock HH:MM even when added to a past or future day. Focus stays in the composer.
Composer Shift+Enter: inserts a newline (default behaviour). Escape in the composer has no local handler, so it bubbles to the window (the shell closes the palette or drawer if open).
The composer draft is a single string shared across days. Switching day keeps the typed text, and pressing Enter then files it under the newly selected day.
Entry click/focus: the textarea becomes editable in place (focus style shows). Typing stores drafts['{iso}:{id}'] = value, and the tag chips under the entry re-derive live from the draft text.
Entry Enter (without Shift): preventDefault and blur, which commits.

Entry Escape: e.stopPropagation() (keeps the shell's window keydown from seeing it), deletes the draft (reverts to the saved text), then blurs on setTimeout 0. Because the re-render happens before the blur, the blur handler sees no draft and does nothing.

Entry blur: if there is no draft, nothing happens. Otherwise val = draft.trim() and the draft is deleted. If val is empty, model.removeNote(iso, id) deletes the note immediately (no confirm, no undo). If val differs from the saved text, model.updateNote(iso, id, val). The note's time stamp is not changed on edit.

Click a tag chip on an entry: tag.open(). A project chip calls model.openProject(pid), switching to the 'workspace' screen for that project (no view-transition, since viaCard is undefined). A routine chip calls model.openRoutine(rid), which sets routineReq {id, t: Date.now()} and switches to the 'routines' screen. There the Routines screen scrolls to [data-rid] (smooth unless reduced) and highlights the row for 1600ms.

Hover an entry row: model.setHover(firstTag.id) if it has any tags. Mouse leave: setHover(null). This is a global 'linked highlight' signal used by other screens (Today/Calendar dim non-matching items to 0.25–0.3 opacity). It has no visible effect on the Notes screen itself.
Hover a Mentions row: setHover(tag.id). Leave: setHover(null). Click: tag.open() (same as the chip).

Click 'Turn this day into an update': if the selected day has at least one note, model.openCheckIn(null, { text: dayText }) opens the Tell Remi drawer (1160px wide, max calc(100% - 160px), slides in from the right) with no focus project and the textarea prefilled. dayText is the day's notes in chronological (insertion) order, one per line: '{HH:MM} {text}'. It contains NO date. The CheckIn textarea focuses at 380ms with the caret at the end. With no notes, the click is a no-op.
Global shortcuts still active on this screen: ⌘K / Ctrl+K toggles the command palette (even while typing in a note textarea). Escape closes the palette or drawer.
Clock: tick() runs on mount and then every 20000ms, updating state.clock only when the HH:MM string changes.
motion: Screen enter/exit (shell-controlled, section wrapper): entering transitions 'opacity var(--dur-base)=240ms var(--ease-out) 60ms, visibility 0s linear 0s' (fade-in with a 60ms delay). Leaving transitions 'opacity var(--dur-fast)=140ms var(--ease-out), visibility 0s linear var(--dur-fast)' (fade-out, then visibility hidden after 140ms). If shell state.instant is true, the transition is 'none'. Screens stay mounted, so state persists across screen switches.
Composer autofocus: 320ms after arriving on the Notes screen.

Day switch (pick): Phase 1 sets fade=true and dir = (n > current ? +1 : -1). The page wrapper animates opacity 1→0 using 'opacity 140ms var(--ease-out)' and transform none→translateY(dir*6px) (a later day drifts down 6px, an earlier day drifts up 6px) using 'transform var(--dur-base)=240ms var(--spring-soft)'. Phase 2 at +120ms (setTimeout) swaps sel and sets fade=false, so the content returns to opacity 1 and transform none with the same transitions. Because the swap happens at 120ms, before the 140ms fade completes, the new day fades in from roughly 5% opacity and settles back from the offset. At +160ms total the composer is focused. Reduced (model.reduced): transform stays 'none' and only the opacity fade runs. Under prefers-reduced-motion, --spring-soft becomes steps(1, jump-start), so the transform resolves instantly while opacity still fades.
Composer hint 'Enter to jot · Shift+Enter…': opacity 0↔1, 'opacity 140ms var(--ease-out)'.

New note 'fresh' highlight: the row background becomes color-mix(in oklch, var(--pc-accent) 7%, transparent). After 1400ms fresh=null and the background returns to transparent via 'background 900ms var(--ease-out)'. Rows are keyed by index (sc-for), so if the day already had notes the existing top row's DOM is reused and the tint FADES IN over 900ms. If the day was empty the new row mounts already tinted (no fade-in). Production: pick one deliberately; likely key by id and animate the tint in quickly (e.g. 140ms), hold, then fade out over 900ms.

Entry row declared transitions 'opacity 220ms var(--ease-out), transform 320ms var(--spring-soft)', but o=1 and t='none' are hard-coded, so no enter animation actually plays (dead scaffold for an intended fade/slide-in of new entries). The design system elsewhere uses the @keyframes remi-settle {from {opacity:0; transform:translateY(6px)} to {opacity:1; transform:none}}, which is a candidate if an entry animation is wanted.
Entry textarea hover/focus: 'background var(--dur-fast)=140ms var(--ease-out)'. The focus ring (inset box-shadow) appears instantly.

WeekSpark bars: 'height var(--dur-slow)=440ms var(--spring-soft)'. They animate when counts change (e.g. after adding a note) or when maxN rescales. Colour changes on selection are instant (no colour transition).
Tag chips, mentions rows, sub line and counts update instantly (no animation).

Drawer opened by the CTA (shell): the panel animates transform translateX(104%)→0 over 'var(--dur-slow)=440ms var(--spring-soft)' with 'opacity var(--dur-base)=240ms var(--ease-out)'. The scrim is color-mix(in oklch, var(--ink) 18%, transparent), fading 240ms ease-out.
algorithms: SELECTED DAY: S = state.sel ?? TODAY; iso = F.iso(S); list = notes[iso] || []; isT = (S === TODAY).

LEFT LIST DAYS: start = TODAY - 27. For n from TODAY down to start: include n if CAL.days[n] exists AND (CAL.days[n].bd OR notes[F.iso(n)] is non-empty). Then, for every key k in notes: n = F.dn(k); include n if n < start AND CAL.days[n] exists AND it is not already included. Future-dated notes (n > TODAY) are never listed. Notes outside the calendar range 2026-08-31..2027-04-30 are never listed. Sort descending.

WEEK HEADERS: for each listed n, mon = n - ((CAL.days[n].w + 6) % 7) (the Monday of that week). If mon !== the previous row's mon, emit a header: 'This week' if mon === TODAY - ((CAL.days[TODAY].w + 6) % 7), else 'Week of ' + F.dm(mon) (e.g. 'Week of 28 Sep').

DAY ROW: label = (n===TODAY ? 'Today · ' : '') + F.s(n). count = arr.length ? String(arr.length) : ''. preview = arr.length ? arr[arr.length-1].text (the latest-added note) : (n===TODAY ? 'Nothing yet today' : 'No notes').

KICKER: if isT, 'Today'. Else if CAL.days[S].bd: ago = CAL.bdDiff(S, TODAY); ago === 1 gives 'Last business day', otherwise ago + ' business days ago'. Else: CAL.days[S].hol || 'Weekend'. (For future BDs ago is negative, which produces e.g. '-1 business days ago', a bug.)

SUB LINE: [d0.bd ? 'BD' + d0.bdm : null, list.length ? list.length + ' note' + (list.length===1?'':'s') : 'no notes yet', mentions.length ? mentions.slice(0,3).map(x=>x.name).join(', ') : null].filter(Boolean).join(' · ').

AUTO-TAGGING tagsFor(text): l = text.toLowerCase(). HARD-CODED project alias table keyed by seed project id: { ret: ['returns pipeline','pipeline','attribution'], manco: ['manco','nav bridge','managing committee'], play: ['playbook','runbook','successor'], fion: ['onboarding','entitlement','fi desk','curve data','bloomberg'], alpha: ['alpha engine','alpha','signal'] }. Step 1, projects (in model.P order): keys = [p.name.toLowerCase(), p.short.toLowerCase(), ...alias[p.id] || []]. If ANY non-empty key is a SUBSTRING of l (String.includes, no word boundaries), push { id: p.id, name: p.short, accent: p.accent, soft: p.soft, open: () => openProject(p.id) }. Step 2, routines (in model.routines order): keys = [name.toLowerCase(), short.toLowerCase(), ...(r.id==='r-ret' ? ['returns','funds'] : r.id==='r-man' ? ['manco pack','bd8'] : [])], then filtered to keys with length > 3 (so 'bd8' is silently dropped). If any key is a substring of l AND NOT (a project tag already matched with id === r.pid AND r.id !== 'r-ret'), push { id: r.id, name: (r.short || r.name) + ' · BAU', accent: 'var(--pc-accent)', soft: 'var(--pc-accent-soft)', open: () => openRoutine(r.id) }. In words: a routine tag is suppressed when its parent project is already tagged, except for the Returns routine, which is always allowed alongside the Returns pipeline project. Output order: projects first, then routines. There is no de-duplication beyond that and no max count.

Worked tagging examples from the seed data: 'Admin files landed at 07:40 this morning instead of last night, so returns started late.' gives [Returns · BAU] (matched via 'returns'). '5 of 12 funds done. Unitranche needed the manual FX fix again, which is exactly what the pipeline should remove.' gives [Returns pipeline (via 'pipeline'), Returns · BAU (via 'funds')]. 'Finance happy to review the ManCo NAV bridge spec on Thursday.' gives [ManCo automation]; the 'ManCo pack' routine does not match because 'manco pack' is absent, and it would be suppressed anyway. 'Recorded the September BD3 run as raw notes for the playbook…' gives [Handover playbook]. 'FI desk suggested Bloomberg curve data…' gives [FI onboarding]. 'Chased the entitlement forms…' gives [FI onboarding].

MENTIONS: for each note in the day's list (chronological), for each tag from tagsFor(note.text) (saved text, not drafts): allTags[tag.id] = allTags[tag.id] || {...tag, count:0}; count++. mentions = Object.values(allTags) sorted by count desc (stable). Each gets count label = count + (count===1 ? ' note' : ' notes'). The count is the number of notes mentioning the target, since a note contributes at most once per id. Seed today: 'Returns · BAU' 2 notes, 'Returns pipeline' 1 note, 'ManCo automation' 1 note.
ENTRIES: [...list].reverse() (newest first by insertion). key = iso + ':' + note.id; v = drafts[key] ?? note.text; tags = tagsFor(v) (live, including unsaved edits).

ADD NOTE (shell addNote): d = new Date(); t = HH(d.getHours() padded to 2) + ':' + MM(d.getMinutes() padded to 2); id = 'n' + Date.now().toString(36); notes[day] = [...(notes[day]||[]), {id, t, text}]; returns id.
UPDATE NOTE: notes[day] = notes[day].map(n => n.id===id ? {...n, text} : n).
REMOVE NOTE: list = notes[day].filter(n => n.id !== id). If list is empty, delete notes[day]; otherwise notes[day] = list.

TOTAL LINE: total = sum of all day arrays' lengths; days = Object.keys(notes).length (every stored day key, including out-of-range ones). Text: total + ' note' + (total===1?'':'s') + ' across ' + days + ' day' + (days===1?'':'s'). Seed: '6 notes across 3 days'.

RECENT NOTES COUNT (for remiNote, and exactly the set CheckIn sends to the AI as recent_notes): recent = CAL.bds.filter(n => n <= TODAY).slice(-5) (the last 5 business days up to and including today). recentN = sum of notes on those days. Seed: Tue 29 Sep, Wed 30 Sep, Thu 1 Oct, Fri 2 Oct, Mon 5 Oct gives 0+0+1+2+3 = 6. CheckIn formats each as F.s(n) + ' ' + note.t + ': ' + note.text, e.g. 'Fri 2 Oct 16:10: Recorded the September BD3 run…'.

WEEK SPARK: mon = TODAY - ((CAL.days[TODAY].w + 6) % 7); wkDays = [mon, mon+1, mon+2, mon+3, mon+4] (calendar days; holidays are not skipped). c = count per day; maxN = Math.max(3, ...counts) (a floor of 3 so a single note isn't a full bar); h = (c/maxN*100) + '%'. bg = n===S ? var(--ink) : c ? var(--ink-faint) : var(--hairline). Label = F.wd(n).slice(0,1) + ' ' + F.d(n) (e.g. 'M 5'). Title = F.s(n) + ' · ' + c + ' note' + (c===1?'':'s').
DAY TEXT (CTA prefill): list.map(n => n.t + ' ' + n.text).join('\n'), in chronological insertion order.
CLOCK: HH:MM from the local Date, polled every 20s, displayed only in today's composer. Other days show '—:—'.

DAY-NUMBER MATH (shell): dn(iso) = Math.round(Date.UTC(y, m-1, d) / 86400000); isoOf(n) = new Date(n*86400000).toISOString().slice(0,10); weekday is taken from getUTCDay(). Monday-of-week = n - ((w + 6) % 7).
backendImplications: ENTITY Note (table notes): id UUID PK; day DATE NOT NULL (the notebook day the note is filed under, which can differ from created_at's date because backfilling past days is allowed); text TEXT NOT NULL (trimmed, non-empty, multi-line allowed); created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL; updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ; plus an ordering key (the created_at or a sequence). The prototype orders within a day by insertion, not by the HH:MM label. Expose time_label 'HH:MM' derived from created_at in the user's timezone (24h). Index on (day).
DELETE-BY-EMPTY semantics: the client treats a blank edited note as a delete. The API should have an explicit DELETE and reject empty text on PATCH (422). The client maps blank-on-blur to DELETE.

ENDPOINTS (api/notes): GET /api/notes?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD returns notes grouped by day (with computed tags). GET /api/notes/days?from&to returns day summaries { date, count, latest_preview, is_business_day, bd_of_month, holiday, week_monday } for the left rail. The rail window is TODAY-27 calendar days plus older days that have notes, so it needs 'all days with notes' plus the business days in the window. GET /api/notes/summary returns { total_notes, total_days } for 'N notes across M days'. POST /api/notes { day, text } returns 201 with the note, time_label and tags. PATCH /api/notes/{id} { text } returns the note with re-derived tags. DELETE /api/notes/{id} returns 204. GET /api/notes/recent?business_days=5 returns the notes on the last 5 business days up to today (used for the rail's 'Remi currently has N recent notes' and server-side for the Tell Remi AI context). GET /api/notes/week?date= returns Mon–Fri counts for the spark, or the client derives this from the range query.

TAGGING SERVICE (services/note_tagging or utils/tagging): move the alias tables out of code into data. Suggested table entity_aliases (id, entity_type 'project'|'routine', entity_id, alias TEXT lowercased), seeded with: ret: returns pipeline, pipeline, attribution; manco: manco, nav bridge, managing committee; play: playbook, runbook, successor; fion: onboarding, entitlement, fi desk, curve data, bloomberg; alpha: alpha engine, alpha, signal; r-ret: returns, funds; r-man: manco pack, bd8 (note that the prototype drops 'bd8' via its length>3 filter). The entity's name and short name are always implicit keys. Keep the rules: case-insensitive substring match; routine keys must be longer than 3 characters; a routine tag is suppressed when its linked project (routine.pid) already matched, unless the routine is flagged to co-tag (in the prototype only r-ret is exempt, so generalise this to a boolean such as routine.co_tag_with_project). Return tags as { target_type, target_id, label ('{short}' or '{short} · BAU'), domain } so the client can pick accent/soft colours.

TAG PERSISTENCE: either compute tags on read (cheap: notes × aliases) or persist a note_mentions table (note_id, target_type, target_id), recomputed on note create/update and whenever aliases, project names or routine names change. The composer needs LIVE tags per keystroke, so ship the alias table to the client (GET /api/aliases, or embed it in a bootstrap payload) and run the same pure matcher client-side to avoid per-keystroke requests. Keep one shared implementation (TS util mirrored in the backend util, or a golden-test fixture), because CheckIn.dc.html's offline simple() parser has its own diverging alias table (ret adds 'returns automation'; fion has 'data access' instead of 'curve data'/'bloomberg'; alpha lacks 'alpha engine'). Unify both on the entity_aliases data.

MENTIONS AGGREGATION per day: GET /api/notes/days/{date}/mentions returns [{ target, label, count_notes }] sorted by count desc (stable). This can also be derived client-side from the day's notes plus tags.

BUSINESS CALENDAR (core/calendar or services/calendar): server-side business-day logic is required: is_business_day, bd_of_month, business-day diff (for 'Last business day' / 'N business days ago'), last-N business days <= today, holiday names (the HOL map is a UK-style placeholder; the user has not yet answered UK vs South Africa). TODAY must come from the real clock in the user's timezone, not a constant.

TELL REMI INTEGRATION: the check-in AI context must include recent_notes = notes from the last 5 business days <= today, formatted '{Ddd d Mon} {HH:MM}: {text}'. Assemble this server-side when proxying the AI call (compliance flag: note text leaves the machine). The 'Turn this day into an update' prefill should include the day's date when the day is not today (the prototype omits it, which would make the AI resolve relative dates against today).

VALIDATION: day must be a valid ISO date. Decide whether future days are allowed (the prototype lets you pick Tue–Fri of the current week via the spark and add notes there, but they then never appear in the left rail). Text is trimmed and non-empty, with a sensible max length (none in the prototype). The id is server-generated (UUID) instead of 'n'+Date.now().toString(36).

PERSISTENCE MIGRATION: the prototype stores notes inside the single localStorage blob 'remi.v1' as { ..., notes: { 'YYYY-MM-DD': [{id,t,text}] }, m2: true }, saved with a 250ms debounce after any state change (errors swallowed) and loaded on boot (falling back to BASE_NOTES). The 'Reset to sample data' palette command restores BASE_NOTES. Provide a one-off import endpoint (POST /api/import/local) that maps {t} to created_at = day + t in the local tz. Remi Home.dc.html also reads remi.v1 to show 'N notes today' (hard-coded to key '2026-10-05'), so it needs GET /api/notes/summary?day=today.

SUGGESTED FOLDERS (per user's architecture): schemas/note.py (NoteCreate{day,text}, NoteUpdate{text}, NoteOut{id,day,time_label,text,created_at,updated_at,tags[]}, DaySummary, MentionOut, TagOut); repositories/note_repository.py (CRUD, range queries, count by day, latest per day); repositories/alias_repository.py; services/note_service.py (create/update/delete, day summaries, recent notes for AI context); services/tagging_service.py (or utils/tagging.py as a pure function); core/calendar.py (business days, holidays, today in the user tz); api/notes.py (routes).
risksAndQuirks: TODAY is hard-coded in the shell (2026-10-05), while the composer clock and addNote timestamps use the real current time. Production must use the real date in the user's timezone everywhere.

addNote always stamps the current wall-clock HH:MM, even when filing a note under a past or future day. Only HH:MM is stored (no date-time), and within-day ordering is insertion order, not time order. A backfilled note at '09:00 today' filed on Fri 2 Oct would show 09:00 and sort after 17:32.

Future days are reachable only through the WeekSpark (Tue–Fri of the current week when today is Monday). The kicker then reads '-1 business days ago' (negative bdDiff bug), and notes added there are hidden from the left rail because the rail only includes n <= TODAY. Fix: either block future days or handle 'Tomorrow' / 'In N business days' and list future days that have notes.
WeekSpark uses 5 consecutive calendar days from Monday with no holiday or business-day check. A holiday Friday still shows a bar.

Routine alias 'bd8' is dead because routine keys are filtered to length > 3. The alias tables are hard-coded to seed ids (ret, manco, play, fion, alpha, r-ret, r-man), so user-created projects and routines only match on name/short. The special-case r-ret suppression exemption is hard-coded.

Substring matching has no word boundaries, which causes false positives: 'alpha' in 'alphabet', 'signal' in any sentence using the word, 'returns' in any returns mention (so every 'returns pipeline' mention also tags 'Returns · BAU'), 'funds' in any funds remark, 'successor' tags the playbook. Consider word-boundary regex and a user-editable alias list.
Routine tag colour is always the PC accent (var(--pc-accent) / var(--pc-accent-soft)) regardless of routine.domain. It should use the routine's domain.
Notes.dc.html and CheckIn.dc.html's simple() hold two DIFFERENT alias tables. Unify them.
The entry enter animation is dead code: o=1 and t='none' are hard-coded although opacity 220ms / transform 320ms spring transitions are declared.

sc-for keys rows by index, so DOM and focus are reused across notes when a new note is prepended. The fresh tint fades in over 900ms on reused rows but appears instantly when the day was empty. In React, key by note.id.

field-sizing: content (the textarea auto-grow) is Chromium-only (Chrome 123+). In Safari and Firefox the rows=1 textareas with overflow:hidden would CLIP multi-line notes. Production needs a JS autosize (e.g. react-textarea-autosize) fallback. This matters because the user is on macOS.
Enter-to-submit has no IME composition guard (e.nativeEvent.isComposing). Add one.
Clearing a note's text and blurring (or pressing Enter) deletes it permanently, with no confirm and no undo. Consider an undo toast.
The composer draft is one string shared across days. Switching day keeps it, so pressing Enter files it under the newly selected day. Drafts (composer and edits) are not persisted across reloads.

style-hover and style-focus are emitted as !important classes. The DayRow hover background overrides the selected row's paper-raised background while hovered (the selected row is still distinguishable by its inset hairline ring and bold label).

model.reduced reflects only the design-tool 'Motion' tweak, not prefers-reduced-motion. The CSS var --spring-soft handles the OS setting for transform easing, but the translate is still applied (it jumps instantly). Production should use a single reduced-motion source (media query plus a user setting).

The CTA stays clickable-looking in size when empty (the bg changes to ink-faint and the cursor to default) but is not disabled (no disabled attribute or aria). Use a real disabled state. There is no hover or active style defined; other primary buttons in the shell use hover bg color-mix(in oklch, var(--ink) 86%, var(--paper)) and active scale(0.98).
dayText prefill omits the date, so 'Turn this day into an update' for a past day sends only times, and the AI resolves relative dates against today.
Hovering entries and mentions sets a global hover id (setHover) with no visible effect on the Notes screen (other screens are hidden). It is harmless but only useful if cross-screen linking is added.
totalLine counts every stored day key, including days outside the CAL range (2026-08-31..2027-04-30) that never appear in the list.
The clock refreshes every 20s, so it can lag the real minute by up to 20s. The note timestamp uses its own new Date() (accurate).
Note ids are 'n' + Date.now().toString(36) (theoretical collision within the same ms). Use server UUIDs.
The seed notes (BASE_NOTES) are demo data and are restored by 'Reset to sample data'. All persistence is the single localStorage key 'remi.v1', debounced 250ms, with errors swallowed silently.

Privacy/compliance: note text is sent as recent_notes to the AI (window.claude / Remi) on every Tell Remi update. The right-rail copy explicitly promises this. The design brief flags that project text leaving the Mac needs compliance sign-off.
Material Symbols Outlined icons used here ('chevron_left', 'edit_note') must be included in the icon subset loaded by the app (the shell's Google Fonts URL subsets icon_names).
localState: sel: number | null (default null). The selected day number; null means TODAY (it auto-follows today). Drives which day's notes, header, composer target, mentions and spark highlight are shown.
draft: string (default ''). Composer text. Drives live draftTags, hint opacity and the Enter-to-add payload. It is shared across day switches.

drafts: Record<'{iso}:{noteId}', string> (default {}). In-progress inline edits per note. They are deleted on blur (commit) or Escape (revert). While present, the entry shows the draft and its live tags.
fresh: noteId | null (default null). The just-added note to tint. Cleared by timeout ft after 1400ms.
fade: boolean (default false). The page transition flag (opacity 0 plus translate while true).
dir: 1 | -1 (undefined initially). Direction of the day switch, which sets the translateY sign (+6px for a later day, -6px for an earlier day).
clock: 'HH:MM' (default ''). Local time for today's composer time column.

Timers: iv = setInterval(tick, 20000) for the clock; ft = the fresh highlight timeout (1400ms); pt = the pick swap timeout (120ms). All are cleared on unmount. There is also a fire-and-forget setTimeout(focus, 320) on arrival and setTimeout(focus, 40) after the swap.
Refs: inRef (composer textarea, for focusing); rootRef (root grid, unused beyond binding).
persistence: Notes live in shell state `notes` (Record<isoDate, Array<{id, t, text}>>), NOT in this component.

The shell persists to localStorage key 'remi.v1' as one JSON blob: { projects, tasks, feed, funds, routines, doneOn, bauDone, notes, m2: true }. The write is debounced 250ms (setTimeout) after componentDidUpdate detects that any of those references changed. Exceptions are swallowed.

Load at boot: loadSaved() parses 'remi.v1' and accepts it only if Array.isArray(s.projects). Then notes = SAVED.notes if present, else BASE_NOTES. There is no notes-specific migration (the m2 migration only affects manco tasks).
resetData() (palette 'Reset to sample data') runs localStorage.removeItem('remi.v1') and restores notes to BASE_NOTES.
Remi Home.dc.html separately reads 'remi.v1' to display the '{n} note(s) today' count from notes['2026-10-05'] (hard-coded date).
Local drafts (composer and edits) and the selected day are in-memory only and survive screen switches (screens stay mounted) but not reloads.
externalCalls: No direct network or AI calls in Notes.dc.html.

Indirect: the 'Turn this day into an update' CTA calls model.openCheckIn(null, { text }). The CheckIn drawer then sends the update to the Remi AI (window.claude in the prototype; see CheckIn.dc.html, whose SYS prompt says: 'recent_notes are the analyst's own jottings from the last few days: use them as background to understand the update, but only propose changes the UPDATE itself supports.'). Its context includes recent_notes built from model.notes over the last 5 business days <= TODAY, formatted 'Fri 2 Oct 16:10: text'.

Fonts (loaded by the shell): Google Fonts Albert Sans (UI), Libre Caslon Text (display: headings, notes, previews), JetBrains Mono (numerics: times, counts, week labels, spark labels), Material Symbols Outlined (icons 'chevron_left', 'edit_note' used here).
copyText: {N} note(s) across {M} day(s)  (e.g. '6 notes across 3 days')
This week  (left-list week header and right-rail section kicker)
Weekend  (or the holiday name, e.g. 'Christmas Day')
Add a note to {Ddd d Mon}…  (placeholder, other days)
Enter to jot · Shift+Enter for a new line
A blank page. Jot anything: a number that looked off, who you are waiting on, what you finished.
Nothing was jotted on this day.
Notes from your last five business days go along with every Tell Remi update, so it knows what you have been doing. Notes never change the plan by themselves.
Turn this day into an update
Opens Tell Remi with these notes filled in, so you can review the changes before anything moves. Remi currently has {N} recent note(s) as background.
No projects or routines named yet. Mention one and it is linked here.
Spark labels '{W} {d}' (e.g. 'M 5'), tooltip '{Ddd d Mon} · {N} note(s)'

actionsInvoked: model.addNote(dayIso, text) -> id. Appends {id:'n'+Date.now().toString(36), t:'HH:MM' now, text} to notes[dayIso] (called from composer Enter).
model.updateNote(dayIso, id, text). Replaces the note text (called on entry blur when the trimmed text changed).
model.removeNote(dayIso, id). Removes the note, and removes the day key when it becomes empty (called on entry blur with empty text).
model.openProject(pid). Closes the palette, then sets screen='workspace', ws=pid, instant=false (no view transition from Notes). Called from project tag chips and mention rows.

model.openRoutine(rid). Sets routineReq={id:rid, t:Date.now()}, screen='routines', instant=false. The Routines screen scrolls to and flashes the row for 1600ms. Called from routine tag chips and mention rows.
model.setHover(id|null). Sets the global linked-highlight id (only when changed). Called on entry and mention hover and cleared on leave.

model.openCheckIn(null, { text: dayText }). Opens the Tell Remi drawer (drawer.open=true, pid=null, session+1, prefill={text}) and closes the palette. Called from the 'Turn this day into an update' CTA when the day has notes.
